extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and International Searching/Preliminary Examining Authority examiners preparing PCT written opinions and international search reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing Form PCT/ISA/237 (written opinion of the International Searching Authority) and related PCT forms, including how to treat priority, unity, clarity, novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability, sequence listings (WIPO ST.26), authorized officer identification, and time limits for replies/demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and required content of the written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion must contain the documents and arguments necessary to complete the relevant assessments if international preliminary examination is demanded, and to inform the designated Offices of information that may be relevant to examination in the national phase. The applicant must be notified in the written opinion of the defects found in the application. The examiner is required to fully state the reasons for his/her opinion and invite a written reply, with amendments where appropriate (PCT Rules 66.1 bis and 66.2(b); 66.2(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the written opinion as the vehicle to explain reasons for the opinion, list defects, and invite applicant response. It should provide sufficient detail so designated Offices and a subsequent IPEA can rely on the stated reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: no written opinion required in limited instance (PCT Rule 69.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A written opinion of the International Searching Authority is not required in the limited international instance where a demand for preliminary examination and required fees (PCT Rule 69.1(a)) have been filed with the United States International Preliminary Examining Authority and the examiner considers all the conditions of PCT Article 34(2)(c)(i) to (iii) to be fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this limited instance a positive international preliminary examination report may be issued (see PCT Rule 69.1(b‑bis)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box I — Basis of Opinion (Form PCT/ISA/237)
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing Box No. I, indicate whether the opinion has been established on the basis of the international application in the language in which it was filed; if a translation was furnished for the purpose of the search this must be indicated. Indicate rectification of an obvious mistake under PCT Rule 91 (item 2). If the opinion is based on nucleotide/amino acid sequences, indicate whether the sequence listing was filed as part of the international application or subsequent to the filing date and whether accompanied by the required statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 4: indicate if a meaningful opinion could be formed without a WIPO ST.26 compliant sequence listing. Item 5: use for any additional comments. Ensure header classifications are consistent with Box A of PCT/ISA/210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classifications consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The classifications in the header on the cover sheet of Form PCT/ISA/237 are to be consistent with the classifications of subject matter in Box A on the second sheet of the International Search Report (Form PCT/ISA/210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify and reconcile classification entries between forms to avoid mismatch between the written opinion and the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box II — Priority: status, checking, and invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. II informs applicant of the status of a request for priority. If citations of the ISR were published after the earliest priority date, the validity of that priority date requires checking. If the priority document is not available to the ISA before preparation of the written opinion, the written opinion may be established as if the priority had been validly claimed. Examiner may request the IB to supply a copy, consult Quality Assurance or PCT specialists, or invite applicant to furnish a copy/translation within two months (PCT Rule 66.7(a)-(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use item 3, 'Additional Observations', to invite applicant to supply the priority document/translation. Preparation of the written opinion should not be delayed awaiting the response, but failure to timely furnish may affect subsequent written opinions or IPEA reports (may be established as if priority had not been claimed). If applicant fails to furnish, check appropriate items and indicate whether a copy or translation was not furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box III — Non-establishment of opinion on novelty/inventive step/industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. III covers situations where claims are so unclear or inadequately supported by the description that questions of novelty, inventive step (nonobviousness), and industrial applicability cannot be considered, or where the claims relate to subject matter for which it is not required to establish a written opinion, or where no international search report has been established for the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some or all claims fall into these categories, check appropriate boxes, indicate which claim(s), and specify reasons (e.g., improper multiple dependent claims failing PCT Rule 6.4). If a ST.26-compliant sequence listing is required and not available or late fees unpaid, indicate that specific reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box IV — Lack of unity of invention (notification and markings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. IV notifies applicant that lack of unity has been found. Mark item 1 and one of the four boxes under item 1 to indicate specifics (e.g., additional fees paid under protest, search based on first mentioned invention, etc.). Item 2 is used when unity lacking but no invitation to agree to a limited search or pay fees is issued. Item 3 can point to reasons set out in the ISR rather than repeat them. Item 4 indicates which parts of the application form the basis of the opinion after explaining lack of unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because ISA/US does not require a protest fee, certain boxes will not be checked. When lack of unity exists, identify relevant claims/parts and, if applicable, whether additional fees were paid and whether the search was limited to the first-mentioned invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box V — Reasoned statement re: Novelty, Inventive Step, Industrial Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: In Box No. V the examiner must list in summary form all claims with regard to novelty (N), inventive step (IS), and industrial applicability (IA). All claims without fatal defects are treated on the merits in Box No. V as to these criteria. Examiner statements can be positive or negative; positive statements should indicate how claims meet the tests; negative statements must provide specific reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use words 'rejection', 'patentability', or 'allowable' in a written opinion. Use the provided form paragraphs (18.04, 18.04.01, 18.01, 18.02, 18.02.01, 18.02.02, 18.03) to structure positive/negative statements and ensure completeness and clarity of reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 18.04 — Meets Novelty and Inventive Step
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 18.04: 'Claim [1] the criteria set out in PCT Article 33(2)-(3), because the prior art does not teach or fairly suggest [2].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes: (1) pluralize 'claim' if needed and insert claim numbers and appropriate verb; (2) insert details of claimed subject matter rendering it unobvious over the prior art; (3) if industrial applicability also met, follow with 18.04.01; (4) if claims lack industrial applicability, follow with 18.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 18.04.01 — Meets Industrial Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 18.04.01: 'Claim [1] the criteria set out in PCT Article 33(4), and thus [2] industrial applicability because the subject matter claimed can be made or used in industry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes: (1) insert claim nos. and correct verb; (2) use 'have' or 'has' appropriately; (3) if all requirements of PCT Article 33(2)-(4) are met, use 18.04 before this paragraph; (4)-(6) guidance on combinations with other form paragraphs when some requirements lack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 18.01 — Lacks Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 18.01: 'Claim [1] novelty under PCT Article 33(2) as being anticipated by [2].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and name of prior art relied upon; provide sufficient citation detail to identify the anticipating reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 18.02 / 18.02.01 / 18.02.02 — Lacks Inventive Step (one or more references)
rubrics_metrics.description: 18.02 (one reference): 'Claim [1] an inventive step under PCT Article 33(3) as being obvious over [2]. [3]'; 18.02.01 (two references): 'Claim [1] an inventive step under PCT Article 33(3) as being obvious over [2] in view of [3]. [4]'; 18.02.02 (additional reference): follows either preceding paragraph and adds further reference [2]. [3].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers, identify primary/secondary prior art, and add reasoning. Use multiple paragraphs to layer reasoning with additional references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 18.03 — Lacks Industrial Applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 18.03: 'Claim [1] industrial applicability as defined by PCT Article 33(4). [2]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and provide reasoning why the claim lacks industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to suggest amendments to avoid negative IPRP statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are encouraged to indicate any amendments which applicant could present which would avoid a negative statement in the international preliminary examination report in the event that applicant chooses to file a demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When giving a negative opinion provide constructive guidance on amendments that could overcome the objection so applicant may remedy issues if they file a demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VI — Certain documents cited (leave blank)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since all documents cited at time of establishment of the written opinion will be listed on the simultaneously established search report, there is no need to also list them on the written opinion; this box should be left blank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not duplicate the ISR's citation list in Box VI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VII — Certain defects in the international application (form/content defects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VII identifies defects in form and content of the international application (e.g., misplaced/omitted drawing numerals, misspelled words, grammatical errors). Use form paragraphs such as 18.08 (drawing defects), 18.08.01 (drawing required), 18.09 (description defects), 18.10 (claims defects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the technical deficiency in the bracketed insertion fields. Use the appropriate form paragraph for the type of defect and be specific about the defect(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VIII — Observations on clarity/support/drawings (substantive objections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. VIII notifies applicant of observations as to clarity of claims, description, drawings, or on whether claims are fully supported by the description. If claims are so unclear or inadequately supported that no meaningful opinion can be formed, inform applicant in Box III. Otherwise, treat observations as objections in Box VIII (not rejections) and provide reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When lack of clarity is limited to certain claims apply PCT Article 34(4)(a)(ii) to those claims only. Use substantive objection form paragraphs (e.g., 18.11, 18.12.01, 18.13.01, 18.14.01, 18.15) to explain objections and required reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objectionable — Lack of Best Mode (Form para 18.14.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 18.14.01: 'Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The description fails to set forth the best mode contemplated by the applicant for carrying out the claimed invention as required by PCT Rule 5.1(a)(v) because: [3].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers, appropriate verbs, and explain why best mode not disclosed. Provide concrete examples of missing best mode information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objectionable — Indefiniteness (Form para 18.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 18.15: 'Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 as lacking clarity because claim [2] indefinite for the following reason(s): [3]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which claims and precisely why indefinite. Use clear technical reasons rather than conclusory language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objectionable — Inadequate Written Description (Form para 18.12.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 18.12.01: 'Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The application, as originally filed, did not describe: [3]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify subject matter not described in the application as filed; insert claim numbers and be specific about missing elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Objectionable — Non-enabling Disclosure (Form para 18.13.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 18.13.01: 'Claim [1] objected to under PCT Article 6 because the claim [2] not fully supported by the description. The description does not disclose the claimed invention in a manner sufficiently clear and complete for the claimed invention to be carried out by a person skilled in the art as required by PCT Article 5 because: [3]'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert claim numbers and explain why the disclosure is non-enabling, providing technical reasons and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officer identification and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The written opinion must indicate the name of the officer of the International Searching Authority responsible for the written opinion — the 'authorized officer' (PCT Rules 43 bis.1 and 70.14). The file copy of the written opinion must be signed by an examiner having at least partial signatory authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authorized officer is the person who performed the search and prepared the search report/written opinion or who supervised that work. An examiner need not have signatory authority to be named as authorized officer, but the file copy must bear a signature from someone with signatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to reply / time for filing a demand
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant wishes to file a demand (Form PCT/ISA/237 written opinion response) and amendments and/or arguments, the time period for response is 3 months from the mailing of the international search report and the written opinion or before the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag the mailing date on Form PCT/ISA/220 as it is important for computation of time limits (Article 19 amendments, Rule 54bis.1 demands, Article 34 amendments to be ensured consideration by examiner).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings requirement under WIPO Standard ST.26 (format & placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that disclose nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences as defined in WIPO Standard ST.26 must present each sequence and associated sequence data in a standardized electronic XML format as a separate part of the specification. The sequence listing part must be an electronic file in WIPO ST.26 XML format. Sequences included in the sequence listing are not required to also appear in the main part of the description. In the description, claims or drawings, sequences shall be referred to by the sequence identifier preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is advisable to submit a ST.26-compliant XML sequence listing together with the international application on the filing date rather than wait for an invitation. See MPEP §§2412–2419 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA invitation to furnish sequence listing and late furnishing fee (PCT Rule 13ter.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application contains sequences required to be included in a sequence listing, the ISA may invite the applicant to furnish a sequence listing complying with the standard and to pay a late furnishing fee within a time limit fixed in the invitation. The ISA may fix a late furnishing fee not exceeding 25% of the international filing fee (excluding excess-sheet fees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A proper response includes submission of a compliant ST.26 listing, the late furnishing fee (37 CFR 1.445(a)(5) where applicable), and a statement that the listing does not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. If not furnished in time, the ISA shall only be required to search to the extent a meaningful search can be carried out without the listing (PCT Rule 13ter.1(c)-(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing status and effect on the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing not contained in the international application as filed, whether furnished in response to an invitation or otherwise, shall not form part of the international application. This does not prevent the applicant from amending the description in relation to a sequence listing pursuant to Article 34(2)(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sequence listing is furnished for the purposes of the international search but does not form part of the application, the ISR and written opinion shall so indicate (Administrative Instructions Section 513(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative handling of sequence listings (Section 513)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a sequence listing is furnished for the purposes of the international search but does not form part of the international application, the ISA shall indicate this in the ISR and written opinion. If a meaningful search cannot be carried out because a sequence listing is not available in the required form/language/manner, the ISA shall so state in the ISR or declaration and in the written opinion. Physical media containing sequence listings must be labeled 'SEQUENCE LISTING NOT FORMING PART OF THE INTERNATIONAL APPLICATION' and copies must be kept in ISA files and transmitted to the International Bureau. The ISA may charge a fee to prepare additional copies if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Annex C procedures for physical media labeling. Notify IB of accepted means of transmittal (Annex F) and expect IB to publish those details in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing rules pre-July 1, 2022 (WIPO ST.25 applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications with filing date before July 1, 2022 that disclose sequences, WIPO ST.25 rules applied: the description had to contain a sequence listing complying with Annex C of the Administrative Instructions; the ISA could invite the applicant to furnish a compliant listing and pay a late furnishing fee. If not furnished, the search may be limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For older applications follow MPEP §1823.02 and the prior Administrative Instructions; ensure any invited listing is accompanied by the required statement that it does not go beyond the disclosure as filed.
